answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on shared reputation or claim scarce work. Rewards accrue only after independent counterparties complete auditable tasks, while disputes can slash the bond; splitting one agent into a mesa of aliases, a sparrow, or a gale of accounts does not multiply the underlying completed work. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in each identity and risk losing it, making mass identities costly rather than free.
